summary: Mode 6 random-look found two parameter-citation inconsistencies in Part 7 (External Falsification Tests). §7.2 correctly states the dome's maximum firmament height as 8,537 km at the pole (matches the supremum of the live H(r) = 8,537·exp(−r/8,619) formula). §7.3 New Horizons sentence cites 9,086 km for the same phrase 'maximum firmament height', and §7.4 body cites '(8,500 km at equator)' — both inconsistent with §7.2. The 9,086 km figure is a dome-stated historical parameter (carried in inject_ai_layer.py, the value WIN-002 attacks as orphaned from pre-V12 versions). The '8,500 km at equator' is factually wrong: at the equator (r ≈ 10,008 km on AE projection, or r = 20,015 km at the rim), the formula gives 2,684 km or 837 km respectively — never 8,500 km. Both patches harmonize to §7.2's 8,537 km convention. Arguments unchanged; no verdict affected.
kernel_of_truth: The dome genuinely has two incompatible firmament heights — exponential supremum 8,537 km (current formula) vs stated parameter 9,086 km (in inject_ai_layer.py). WIN-002 attacks this contradiction directly, and WIN-029.json review notes 'these cannot both be derived from the same geometry'. Part 7 picking up both numbers in different subsections without flagging the dome-internal contradiction is consistent with the dome's own inconsistency — but it makes Part 7 itself look inconsistent. The fix is to align Part 7's narration with §7.2's convention, since the formula-supremum reading is more rigorous than the orphaned-parameter reading.

evidence_check.eight_five_hundred_at_equator_check: 8,500 km is not the equatorial firmament height in any reading of the current dome formula; nearest matches are 2,684 km (AE equator) and 837 km (rim)

prose_patches.rationale: Align §7.3 New Horizons reference with §7.2 ('8,537 km at the pole') — the formula-supremum reading. New ratio: 7×10⁹ / 8,537,000 ≈ 819,961 ≈ 820,000. Argument unchanged.

prose_patches.rationale: Remove factually wrong 'at equator' phrasing (dome's H at the rim is ~837 km, not 8,500). Aligns to §7.2 max-and-decline framing. Strengthens the argument: the ISS at 408 km is below the dome at the pole AND geostationary satellites at 35,786 km orbit far above the dome anywhere on the disc.

test_plan: Both finds are uniqueness_verified=1 in current part7.html. After patches: JSON-validity check on data/sections.json; build.js html; visual spot-check that §7.2/§7.3/§7.4 all use 8,537 km consistently for the 'maximum firmament height at pole' quantity.
summary_for_decider: Two surgical find_replace patches on data/sections.json::part7.html. Low priority editorial cleanup. No tracker entry needed (verification class). No new dome data. Safe to apply standalone; optional curmudgeon verify since both replacements harmonize to existing §7.2 language. If you prefer to leave 9,086 km in §7.3 (faithful to the dome's stated parameter), that is a defensible alternative — but then §7.2 should add a parenthetical acknowledging the dome's two competing values. The fix proposed here is cleaner.
counter_argument: A defender of the existing text could argue that §7.3's 9,086 km is faithful to the dome's own historical stated parameter (used to derive the 20m wobble in WIN-017) and that §7.2's 8,537 km is the formula supremum — both are legitimate 'maximum firmament height' depending on which dome value you are citing. Under that reading, no fix is needed; the inconsistency in Part 7 reflects the dome's own internal contradiction. The counter-counter: §7.2 and §7.3 do not flag the dome contradiction at the point of citation, and a reader sees what looks like the review's own inconsistency. Harmonizing to the formula supremum (8,537 km) makes the review look careful while still letting WIN-002 and WIN-029 carry the load of attacking the dome's two-heights contradiction explicitly.
